Hi Andrew — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attachments/links below:

- Retention: Default prompt/interaction logs are retained for 30 days (rolling) for hosted accounts. Customers on Dedicated or Private deployments can configure retention to as-low-as 0 days (ephemeral) or longer windows via contract.
- Training: Redwood DOES NOT use customer prompts or prompt-derived content for improving or fine-tuning models without explicit, documented opt-in. Opt-in is a contractual flag; there is a managed process (Legal + Product) before any customer data is included in training corpora.
- Evidence: We can provide deletion audit logs and a redacted sample export demonstrating a standard retention cycle. See attached summary and a Drive bundle we will share with your security team.

I attached a concise SIG answer PDF and an evidence pointer. If you prefer, Marissa (security/compliance) can provide the deletion audit extract and attestations.

Next steps: If you confirm you want the deletion audit CSV and the SOC 2 reference pack, I will loop Marissa and drop the Drive link.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Hi Andrew / Vanessa — looping in compliance to provide the evidence package. Quick attestation summary and what we attached/linked:

- Data categories and retention: By default for hosted accounts we retain:
  * raw prompt text (30 days)
  * model outputs/completions (30 days)
  * KV cache entries: ephemeral, tied to session lifecycle; default eviction at 1 hour, not persisted to long-term storage for hosted customers
  * Aggregated telemetry (30 days, aggregated metrics only)

- Training: We do not include any customer-identifiable prompts or outputs in training corpora unless there is an explicit opt-in (contract clause: RD-TRAIN-OPTIN) and a documented data ingestion ticket. Opt-in is visible in two places: the contract clause and a portal flag in the customer settings (flag id: training_consent_v1).

- Evidence provided: attached redwood_deletion_audit_q1_2027.csv (redacted) shows a sample record lifecycle with timestamped deletion at day 31. Also shared a Drive folder with SOC 2 summary, SIG answer PDF, and the deletion audit (link below).
